messages:
Maya K: quick Q — we want to share a batch of eval outputs with VendorX for model tuning. Some prompts are user-submitted and might include emails/addresses/phone numbers. Allowed? what classification + redaction level do we need?
Ana S: short answer: not raw PII. If outputs can contain PII, treat as Confidential. Do not send raw logs. Vendor must sign DPA + access controls.
Ravi P: FYI the eval set is ~12k rows, ~2% have contact info. We use automated scrubbers but they sometimes miss odd formats. Want to keep context around the placeholder to preserve eval signal.
Jordan L: legal: we need a DPIA check if vendor processes personal data at scale. Also ensure vendor's subprocessors are listed in DPA. If data is purely synthetic or pseudonymized and irreversible, it's lower risk.
Maya K: what counts as "pseudonymized" here? Is hashing emails okay?
Ana S: hashing alone is reversible if salt leaked; it's still personal data under most regs. Better: remove direct identifiers and replace with neutral tokens like <EMAIL_REDACTED>, <PHONE_REDACTED>. If you need continuity for dev work, use synthetic surrogates generated from a non-production generator and log mapping in a secured vault — only if absolutely necessary and approved.
Ravi P: procedural question: do we need an internal access approval ticket for the vendor export? I can stub a pipeline that outputs scrubbed JSON.
Ana S: yes — open an infra/access ticket listing exact dataset names, scrub steps, and vendor account IDs. Include sample of 5 representative rows (sanitized) for review. Security will check redaction effectiveness.
Maya K: I'll open the ticket. Proposed scrub step we'll run first: regex replace for emails, phones, credit-card-like patterns, then run a second heuristic pass to remove name-like tokens. snippet: ````js
// simplified scrub example
const scrub = (text) => text.replace(/\b[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,6}\b/g, '<EMAIL_REDACTED>')
  .replace(/\b\d{3}[- ]?\d{3}[- ]?\d{4}\b/g, '<PHONE_REDACTED>')
  .replace(/\b\d{4}[- ]?\d{4}[- ]?\d{4}[- ]?\d{4}\b/g, '<CC_REDACTED>')
  // additional heuristics
  ;
````
Ana S: looks fine as a starting point. We'll run it on the sample and do a manual pass. Also add a checksum/audit header to each exported file and ensure S3 ACLs are locked to vendor's bucket with restricted KMS.
sec-bot: audit-log created: access-review-ticket-4382 (assigned to Ana S).
Jordan L: flag — vendor contract needs to explicitly prohibit downstream sharing and require deletion confirmation after project end. Add that to the ticket notes.
Maya K: great. Plan: I'll prepare sanitized sample + scrub pipeline, open access ticket + attach vendor DPA copy. Will ping here when ticket is up.
Ana S: thanks — once ticket is up we'll do a quick redaction QA and sign off. :white_check_mark:
